assertions.name: saturated_binding_fraction_approaches_hbar_q_sq
assertions.source: The mass-difference cancellation predicts B/A/m_N ≈ ℏ_q² at saturation; AME ⁵⁶Fe gives 0.7 < (B/A/m_N)/ℏ_q² < 1.1 (measured ≈0.9). Scope-(a) forward observation under the numerology guard — the analytic dichotomy is Lean-proved, but the exact ℏ_q² saturation value is not derived (open kernel). No fit.

description: Derivation attempt for the mass/binding ℏ_q-rung split (item 3b→1 crux). Step 1 (corpus trace): the mass multiplier's 1/ℏ_q² is the CAL-2 muon-anchor cusp factor (m_μ/m_e = Vol(4₁)/ℏ_q²), which the binding ansatz B = m_e·Vol·M does not re-apply. Step 2 (Lean, sorry-free QOU.Mass.BindingMassRung): the analytic dichotomy is proved — mass multiplier is an order-2 pole with residue lw, binding/mass = (M/lw)·ℏ_q² → 0 at the classical point. Step 3 (physical prediction test): the mass-difference cancellation predicts the saturated nuclear binding fraction B/A/m_N ≈ ℏ_q²; AME data rise toward ℏ_q² with A, reaching ≈0.9·ℏ_q² at ⁵⁶Fe (ℏ_q²≈0.982% ≈ empirical ~0.9%/nucleon). VERDICT: the rung factor is traced to CAL-2 and the dichotomy is Lean-proved, but a first-principles proof that binding saturates at EXACTLY ℏ_q² (not merely O(ℏ_q²)) is the OPEN KERNEL (beaned); the 0.9·ℏ_q² match is scope-(a) under the numerology guard. No fit; no wiring; q₀ proton-anchored.
